sights.w: A former landfill three times the size of Central Park being remade into rolling meadows and marsh; North Park opened in 2023 with a parking lot, trails and bike stations.
One of the only authentic classical Chinese scholar's gardens in the United States, built by artisans from Suzhou, tucked inside the Snug Harbor botanical grounds.

sights.address: 2453 Arthur Kill Rd, Staten Island, NY 10309
sights.w: A working marine scrapyard on the Arthur Kill where the rusting hulls of roughly 100 tugs, ferries and barges sit half-sunk in the mud; view it from the roadside, not the fenced yard.
A lavish 2,800-seat Spanish-Baroque movie palace from 1929, restored in 2004 and now a nonprofit stage for national touring concerts, comedy and dance a short walk from the ferry.
A c.1840 Gothic Revival cottage that sheltered inventor Antonio Meucci and Italian revolutionary Giuseppe Garibaldi, now an Italian-American cultural museum in Rosebank.
Staten Island's oldest and largest active cemetery, dating to 1740, spread across 113 acres on Todt Hill and home to the private granite Vanderbilt family mausoleum.
A quiet South Shore park where a freshwater pond sits behind a beach on Raritan Bay, with woodland trails, a playground and one of the island's better spots for shore birding.
A pocket wilderness of kettle ponds, streams and marsh laced with five hiking trails; a small nature center runs naturalist-guided walks that leave on Sunday afternoons.
New York City's first outlet center, an open-air complex of brand shops and eateries on the St. George waterfront steps from the ferry terminal, with harbor views back toward Manhattan.

food.address: 750 Port Richmond Ave, Staten Island, NY 10302
food.w: A Port Richmond institution long rated among the North Shore's best pizzerias, its thin-crust pies once featured on Bobby Flay's Throwdown.
A Bulls Head Sri Lankan kitchen from the family behind the old San Rasa, chopping griddled kottu roti and ladling fiery curries in the island's Sri Lankan corridor.

food.address: 4254 Arthur Kill Rd, Staten Island, NY 10309
food.w: A tavern operating on this Charleston site since 1855, serving sauerbraten, schnitzel and steins of German beer in a carved-wood old-world dining room and biergarten.
A classic Italian bakery on Hylan Boulevard baking its own bread on premises, prized for savory lard bread studded with prosciutto and pecorino alongside pastries and sandwiches.

food.address: 461 Port Richmond Ave, Staten Island, NY 10302
food.w: A Mexican restaurant and bakery anchoring Port Richmond's Little Mexico, open daily for tacos, guisados and pan dulce baked in-house.
A St. George spot near the ferry cooking West African plates of jollof rice, stews and soups, a foothold of the island's Liberian and African community.
